findings.claim: A project-level .claude/agents file is a different trust class from a plugin agent. The host honours fields (hooks, mcpServers, permissionMode) that plugin agents ignore, as spec.md Clarifications quotes from the host sub-agents doc. The recipe copies a whole file, so a user, or a newcomer pasting from a blog or a PR, can add those keys as easily as editing tools. FR-003 names three allowed keys but never says other keys are privileged, so the reader cannot see where the line is. Shipped files carry only model, memory, color, so nothing the chorus ships crosses it today. Remedy: add one README sentence to FR-003 and T003, saying that hooks, mcpServers and permissionMode run with the user's authority and plugin agents ignore them. No checker, because nobody can operate one at the stated capacity.

evidence.note: FR-003 limits changes to model, effort, tools but does not mark other keys as privileged.
T003 repeats the recipe without the privileged-key line.

findings.pull_quote: The copy changes who the file is trusted as, and the recipe does not say so.

findings.claim: Widening `tools` is a capability grant by file edit. It is invisible in the review record (the Q-33 narrowing) and never refreshed. The threat is self-inflicted, because the person who edits the file is the person whose tools are granted, so no attacker crosses a boundary there. A README warning is the right and only affordable control. A detector, record field or lint would be unearned and would turn into theatre. The one case that matters is a shared repo, where a teammate's committed copy widens tools for everyone who clones it. Remedy: say in the README that a committed .claude/agents copy is reviewed like code. Keep the feature docs-only.

evidence.note: The acceptance scenario lets the file set a tool list.
The accepted cost covers the fork but not the committed-copy case.

findings.pull_quote: A grant you make to yourself needs a warning, not a detector.

findings.claim: Both the shipped file and a same-name copy declare `memory: project`, and the body writes to .claude/agent-memory/<name>/ (agents/kent-beck-persona.md:132). That folder is committed and published (addendum section 5). The copy adds no new path but adds a new author: a project that retunes a reviewer on a private codebase will have that reviewer saving findings from the codebase into a published directory. The recipe's 'keep the body' preserves the instruction without telling the reader why it matters. Remedy: one hygiene sentence in FR-004 or T003 saying the copy writes to the same public memory folder, so private material stays out of it.

evidence.note: The body directs memory writes to .claude/agent-memory/<name>/.
Persona memory is public; records cite private material by reference only.

findings.pull_quote: The retune changes the model, but the memory folder stays public.

findings.claim: Checked, no finding. install.sh writes and prunes only paths recorded in $CLAUDE_HOME/.chorus-install-manifest, and refuses any path that is not relative and inside CLAUDE_HOME. A copy in <project>/.claude/agents is outside CLAUDE_HOME and never enters the manifest, so the installer neither overwrites nor prunes it. The only residual risk is staleness, which FR-004 already accepts.

evidence.note: Prune loop skips unrecorded paths and refuses paths outside CLAUDE_HOME.
The differs-kept branch leaves edited files alone.

findings.pull_quote: The installer never reaches the copy, so the risk is staleness, not damage.

findings.claim: Top recommendation. The recipe gets to touch what the plugin did not: a file loaded as the user's own, with the user's tools, in a repo others may clone. The cheapest control with the best return is README sentences, no code. Fold F41 (privileged keys), F42 (committed copies are reviewed like code) and F43 (the copy shares the public memory folder) into T003 as three sentences. A checker or record field would fail the poverty line. The sentences hold when nobody maintains them, because nothing in them requires operation.

evidence.note: T003 is where the three sentences land.

evidence.ref: Security poverty line (Nather), applied at gate #8: no countable maintainer capacity
evidence.note: Price every control at no operator capacity.

findings.pull_quote: Three sentences hold when no one maintains them; a checker does not.
